statement: Which of these words looks exactly the same after the page is turned upside down with a half turn?

choices.misconception: I picked MOM because it reads the same backwards, but a half turn changes each M into a W.
I thought E looks the same upside down, but a half turn makes it face the other way.
I checked that T is the same on both sides, but upside down its bar ends up at the bottom.
I thought D stays a D upside down, but a half turn makes its curved side face left.

hints: A half turn changes two things about a word, not just one.
Turning a word upside down reverses the order of the letters and also turns each letter over. Check both: the reversed word must match, and every letter must still be itself after a half turn.
Reading backwards is not enough. Test each letter: does M stay M upside down? Does N stay N? Does O?

solutions.reliable: A half turn puts the last letter first and also turns each letter upside down. All five words read the same backwards, so the order is fine for each; the test is the letters. M becomes W, E faces the other way, T has its bar at the bottom and D faces left. N and O both look the same after a half turn, so NOON is unchanged. The transferable idea: a half turn reverses order and rotates each piece, so check the pieces as well as the order.

whyOnTest: Half-turn symmetry is not the same as reading backwards, and every distractor here reads the same backwards.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
